body:
A public elliptic-curve key is a point obtained by repeatedly adding a known point to itself. Recovering the number of additions is the discrete-logarithm problem. Shor’s algorithm supplies the quantum route; the question here is what it takes to execute that route on an error-corrected machine.

Compiled model · one attempt

Recover the secret scalar \(d\) from the public point \(Q=[d]P\) on secp256k1, where \(P\) is a known generator.

19,397physical qubits
25.690days per attempt

The headline 63.3% success estimate combines heuristic classical recovery with modeled hardware reliability. The conservative branch gives 40.7%, conditional on classical search covering the omitted 48 bits. How the probabilities combine →

The interesting question

The arithmetic is mostly serial. More magic-state factories alone cannot make it fast: the compiler must move data, clear corrections, and perform each logical measurement quickly. The paper makes those costs explicit on one device.

From a hidden scalar to a measurement schedule

The first step is to encode the secret in a Fourier relation. Evaluating that relation requires many reversible point additions. A classical table supplies each window’s known point; the quantum circuit must load it coherently, add it, and erase temporary information without disturbing interference.

The expensive division inside a point addition leads to the first major saving: record the gcd decisions and replay them. The record applies an inverse without holding a separate inverse register. Short arithmetic and randomized masks save further work, with their effect on success controlled by an explicit amplitude bound.

Those gates still need somewhere to run. The compiler moves registers while arithmetic is underway, and the architecture clears Clifford frames in idle blocks. Finally, direct CCZ factories supply the resource consumed by each Toffoli. Together these choices connect an arithmetic circuit to a timed sequence of physical measurements.

Where the time goes

The scheduled multiplication and lookup layers account for most of the runtime. Each bar below multiplies the corresponding layer count by the same 0.0294958-second duration; the comparison concerns this compiled schedule and timing model.

Multiplication and lookup dominate. The relevant totals are 40.42 million compiled Toffoli injections and 75.25 million measurement layers; they measure different costs.

Choose a route

Follow the paper from its introduction, or start with the Fourier relation and continue through the arithmetic. Every paper section, appendix, and essential borrowed construction still has its own page. Open derivations when needed; source coverage and limitations are collected separately.

title: Breaking 256-bit elliptic-curve signatures: a circuit-to-hardware study

body:
Two moduli, two jobs

Here \(P\) is a known generator point, \(Q\) the public key point, and \([d]P\) denotes \(d\)-fold group addition. The estimate concerns one quantum key-recovery attempt, not every task required to compromise a running system.

The discrete logarithm is the scalar \(d\) in \(Q=[d]P\). The curve secp256k1 uses

\[y^2=x^3+7\pmod p,\qquad p=2^{256}-2^{32}-977.\]
Coordinates

\(x,y\in\mathbb F_p\): field arithmetic wraps modulo the prime \(p\).

Scalars

\(d\in\mathbb Z_r\): point multiples wrap modulo the order \(r\) of \(P\).

What a complete estimate connects

The circuit specifies reversible operations. The compiler assigns logical qubits—encoded degrees of freedom—to code blocks and schedules compatible measurements. The architecture implements those measurements with physical ions, error checks, transport, and prepared resource states.

The missing unit is a measurement layer

A Toffoli count measures non-Clifford resource consumption. A measurement layer counts operations the device can execute simultaneously. Removing an arithmetic ancilla or moving a register can cost layers without consuming another Toffoli state.

\[\underbrace{T}_{\text{runtime}}=\underbrace{D}_{\text{scheduled layers}}\;\underbrace{\tau}_{\text{seconds per layer}}.\]

The reported \(D=75{,}251{,}329\) and \(\tau=0.0294958\,\mathrm{s}\) give 616.555 hours, or 25.690 days. The difficult result is the legal schedule underlying \(D\).

The device being estimated

The proposed trapped-ion design uses a reference two-qubit Pauli error scale of \(10^{-4}\), with separate rates and durations for its other operations. It charges every logical measurement at the Toffoli-layer duration. Those assumptions define the estimate; the overview shows which design changes make that duration small.

title: I. Introduction: what does a complete resource estimate count?

body:
Match the machine to a serial circuit

The target is the secret scalar \(d\) in \(Q=[d]P\), with \(P,Q\) known curve points. A Clifford frame stores unapplied Clifford gates classically, changing later measurement observables. A Pauli representative is a physical operator implementing the desired encoded observable.

In the baseline Walking Cat architecture, the paper implements a Toffoli using seven T states, where a T state supplies the gate \(T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})\). Preparing more such states does not remove the latency of injecting and correcting them.

Design choiceWhat changesWhy it helps
Direct CCZ statesOne three-qubit resource per ToffoliShorter injection sequence
Disjoint Pauli supportsThree joint parities measured togetherOne measurement layer
Idle frame clearingCorrect upcoming blocks in advanceLess blocking on the serial path
Integrated routingCompute while relocating registersFewer separate movement layers

Supply is only half the timing problem

Supply

Four factories: under 28 ms per accepted CCZ state on average.

Consumption

At most one CCZ per charged 29.5 ms layer.

The resource state is \(|\mathrm{CCZ}\rangle=\mathrm{CCZ}|+\rangle^{\otimes3}\). Two Hadamards on the target turn a CCZ into a Toffoli. Parallel injection requires physically disjoint Pauli representatives in each block; commutation alone is insufficient. See the support diagrams.

Count capacity and workspace separately

The memory code Q102 has parameters \([[102,22,9]]\): 102 data ions encode 22 logical qubits at distance 9. Sixty-nine memory blocks provide 1,518 slots for a circuit peaking at 1,457 logical qubits. Four additional blocks clear Clifford frames; factories, cats, and loss-replacement ions complete the 19,397-ion inventory.

Approximation is a resource

Shorter carry propagation and phase repair save gates. For ideal success \(P_0\) and per-input oracle failure bound \(p_f\), averaged over masks and cleanup outcomes,

\[P_{\rm alg}\ge\bigl(\max\{0,\sqrt{P_0}-2p_f\}\bigr)^2,\qquad p_f\le0.03346.\]

The loss in success amplitude is linear in \(p_f\). The proof explains why phase errors must be counted too.

The repeated unit

Sixteen-bit lookup windows, a direct initial lookup, and a 48-bit omission leave 28 point additions. Each addition uses two in-place multiplications and three coordinate lookups: these dominate runtime.

The final probability

Approximate arithmetic reduces ideal algorithm success; modeled hardware survival reduces it again. The heuristic recovery branch gives 63.3%. The 40.7% branch starts from a rigorous Fourier bound and assumes classical search covers the omitted-window ambiguity. Appendix E performs the complete accounting.

title: II. Overview: connect circuits, schedules, and hardware

body:
What carries beyond this estimate

Three ideas generalize: record only the decisions needed to reverse arithmetic; combine movement with computation; and prepare the non-Clifford resource that the application consumes. Their value appears in the scheduled measurement depth, not just a smaller gate count.

Limitations

Assumption or gapDecisive next check
Full-device transport, timing, and swap-loss modelValidate long-duration behavior with a more detailed trap-and-loss model.
Independent hardware-failure categoriesModel correlated failures; compare the 26.46% product estimate with the 27.44% union bound.
Classical recovery after omitting 48 bitsSpecify search cutoffs and measure classical runtime. The main table charges the quantum schedule.
Internal compiler and noise simulationsRelease schedules, decoder settings, simulator inputs, and error samples for independent reproduction.

The approximately 20,000-ion device is proposed. Its specified fidelities, loading, transport, and decoding behavior are assumed throughout each attempt. The 63.3% end-to-end branch also uses heuristic classical recovery; the 40.7% branch requires recovery search covering the shortened-register ambiguity.

Where further optimization could matter

All logical measurements receive the same conservative duration, and memory blocks are treated as active throughout. A schedule with operation-specific timing and a different space–time allocation could change the tradeoff. Applying the compiler and direct CCZ factory to another arithmetic-heavy algorithm would test how much depends on this circuit’s serial structure.

Per attempt is not time to success

A logical fault changes encoded information; a physical fault need not. For independent attempts with success probability \(s\), negligible reset cost, and a classically checkable answer,

\[\Pr(\text{success by attempt }m)=1-(1-s)^m,\qquad \mathbb E[T_{\rm first}]=T/s.\]

The reported 25.690 days is \(T\), the duration of one attempt. Substituting the rounded heuristic success \(s=0.633\) gives about 40.6 quantum-compute days to the first success on average; \(s=0.407\) gives about 63.1 days. These derived expectations use the independent-attempt assumptions above and exclude classical recovery time.

body:
Symbols and their roles

[[notation]]

Circuit and measurement conventions

Read gates from left to right. A wire labeled by an integer or a curve point is a whole register; a curve-point wire bundles coordinate registers. A filled dot is a quantum control, a circled plus an X target, and dashed paths carry classical results. Boxes labeled by arithmetic maps are subroutines, not elementary gates.

A Pauli readout bit \(m\) denotes eigenvalue \((-1)^m\). An X readout can be implemented by Hadamard then Z readout. A correction with exponent \(m\) is applied only for \(m=1\). A wire initialized at zero is promised clean workspace; returning it to zero requires uncomputation or measurement with phase correction.
